headline: Funding flows. Partnerships form. Delays persist.
deck: This week, space funding continues to surge while partnerships are formed to tackle inefficiencies.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This cash influx is designed to enhance its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, a sector that’s gaining traction with defense contracts. DoD pull-through is now the headline, with the Pentagon keen on tracking threats in orbit.
stories.soWhat: In an era where space is the new frontier for defense, True Anomaly's funding is a clear signal that the government is ready to invest heavily in surveillance capabilities.

stories.head: Fotrastra and Hadrian team up for satellite efficiency
stories.body: Fotrastra and Hadrian have announced a partnership aimed at streamlining satellite production processes. The collaboration reflects a growing trend in the industry where efficiency is prioritized, as both companies look to reduce costs and time-to-market for their satellite offerings. Given the high stakes of satellite deployment, this could set a new standard for production timelines.
stories.soWhat: If this partnership succeeds, it might force competitors to rethink their own production strategies, which could ripple through the satellite supply chain.

stories.head: Boeing still waiting on Starliner flight schedule
stories.body: Boeing continues to negotiate with NASA regarding the schedule for its next Starliner flight, highlighting the ongoing challenges in the commercial crew program. The delays have raised questions about Boeing's ability to meet its contractual obligations and maintain its competitive edge in the space launch sector. Meanwhile, SpaceX continues to forge ahead with its own crewed missions.
stories.soWhat: At this point, it’s clear that patience is a virtue in space—Boeing may need more than just rockets to get back in the game.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on hypersonic tests
watchlist.body: With the hypersonic glide-vehicle test delayed for the third consecutive quarter, the implications for military readiness are becoming increasingly concerning.

watchlist.title: Watch for developments in satellite partnerships
watchlist.body: As Fotrastra and Hadrian's partnership unfolds, other companies may follow suit to enhance their production capabilities, potentially reshaping the satellite market.

watchlist.title: Funding trends to monitor next week

talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
